# Neper — full summary for agents

Neper is a general-purpose programming language optimized end to end for software written
by LLM agents. It is MIT open source, 100% self-hosted (compiler, linker and standard
library are written in Neper), and it builds deterministic native binaries for Windows,
Linux and macOS on CPU and GPU.

The design targets, published and measured in the repository and blog, are one million
lines per second per core and a sub-second whole-project rebuild. The toolchain aims to
give an agent everything between prompt and binary as one system: causal diagnostics,
hermetic tests, a byte-identical self-hosting fixed point, no VM and no GC runtime in the
image. One language covers CPU and GPU kernels.

Canonical URLs:

- Website: https://neper.dev/
- Get started: https://neper.dev/get-started.html
- Showcase: https://neper.dev/ux/showcase.html
- Repository: https://github.com/nebosa-company/neper
- Discord: https://discord.gg/AdRneEsbCu
- llms.txt: https://neper.dev/llms.txt
- Sitemap: https://neper.dev/sitemap.xml

## Language essentials

Neper source is UTF-8, declarations start at column 0, blocks use braces and statements
are newline-separated; comments are `//`.

Every alphabetic terminal is a keyword and may not name a value, type, field or module:
`as` `break` `case` `const` `continue` `default` `defer` `else` `enum` `error` `extern`
`false` `fn` `for` `if` `in` `isize` `let` `nil` `nocheck` `ok` `own` `resource` `ret`
`shared` `struct` `switch` `true` `try` `type` `undef` `union` `unreachable` `use`
`usize` `var` `when` `while` `zero`.

Naming: functions, values, fields and modules use `snake_case`; types use `PascalCase`;
constants use `SCREAMING_SNAKE`. A local may not shadow a module-scope name or a builtin
(E-NAME-0003).

Types are explicit and literals are typed: `0u32`, `0usize`, `0.0f64`, `0u8`. Every
numeric conversion is written out, never implicit. `zero` is the zero value of a type and
`undef` is an uninitialised value. Errors are values: a function returning `err` reports
success with `ret ok` and a named `error X` with `ret X`; `try` propagates. Strings are
slices of `u8` but must hold UTF-8; raw strings are `r#"..."#`.

Memory is arena-based. `mem.alloc[T](a, count)` returns a slice and an error;
`mem.mark`/`mem.reset` frame a unit of work. Slices and pointers are explicit; there is no
garbage collector.

The standard library is imported by module: `use e.io`, `use e.os`, `use e.mem`,
`use e.math`, `use e.data.list as list`, `use e.text.regex as regex`, `use e.ui`,
`use e.gpu`, and so on. Platform modules live under `lib/e/os`, `lib/e/x` for external
libraries, and `lib/e/gpu` for the CPU/GPU kernel model.

Example:

```neper
use e.io

fn main(args: []str) -> err {
    try io.print("Hello, Neper")
    ret ok
}
```

Program entry points accept either `fn main(args: []str) -> err` or
`fn main(a: *mem.Arena, args: []str) -> err`; an integer-returning `main() -> i64` is also
accepted, where a non-zero result is a non-zero process status.

## Toolchain

- `neper run file.e`: compile and run in one step.
- `neper build file.e -o out.exe`: build an executable.
- `neper check file.e`: check only, with the same diagnostics.
- `neper emit-executable <main.e> <repo-root> <arch> <os> <out> [--gpu glsl]`: emit an
  executable directly (the form the self-host fixtures use).
- `--release`, `--incremental`, `-j N` and `--arena SIZE` shape optimisation, reuse,
  parallelism and the compiler's working arena.

Diagnostics carry an identity such as `E-NAME-0003` or `E-TYPE-0003` with a span and the
expected/found values, so a repair can be made from the message alone. The full list is in
`docs/diagnostics.md`.

## Crawler policy

`robots.txt` allows every crawler, including AI crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot,
ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended). `llms.txt` is the short curated index for
agents and `llms-full.txt` (this file) is the long one; both link the canonical page for
each topic.
